seo.title: Homeless help in Philadelphia - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people experiencing homelessness or a housing crisis in Philadelphia: shelter, meals, health care, benefits, work, identification, and legal support.

page.heading: Philadelphia homeless and housing-crisis help
page.urgent: Immediate danger, police, fire, or ambulance: 911 Street outreach for a person living outdoors: 215-232-1984, 24 hours Food, shelter, benefits, and local referrals: 211 or 866-964-7922; text 898211 Mental-health or substance-use crisis: call or text 988, or call 215-685-6440 Domestic-violence crisis: 866-723-3014, confidential and available 24 hours — sms:898211
page.notice: Beds, meals, funding, routes, hours, and eligibility can change. Call or check the linked provider page before traveling when possible. No listing guarantees a bed, meal, treatment, payment, benefit, housing, or job. Call 911 for immediate danger or a medical emergency.
page.intro:
Philadelphia has different shelter intake locations for families, single men, single women, veterans, and young adults. Tell staff your household members, age, gender identity, health or mobility needs, pregnancy, safety concerns, service animal or pet, and whether you need transportation. Ask for a backup plan if no bed is available.
Best first step: during weekday daytime hours, visit Appletree Family Center or Roosevelt Darby Center for assessment. After hours, use the intake location matching your household below. For someone living outdoors, call Street Outreach at 215-232-1984. Placement depends on current capacity and assessment.
page.footer: No Home Help is a volunteer-maintained directory, not an emergency service or service provider.

categories.title: Urgent help, outreach, and severe weather

entries.title: Emergency services — 911
entries.description:
Phone: 911.
Call for immediate violence, fire, overdose, unconsciousness, severe breathing trouble, heavy bleeding, serious injury, or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location or nearest landmark and describe the danger first.
City of Philadelphia — safety and emergencies

entries.title: Homeless Street Outreach Hotline
entries.description:
Phone: 215-232-1984, 24 hours.
Call for a person living outdoors who may need shelter, transport, medical care, behavioral-health help, or treatment. Give the exact location, clothing description, observed condition, and immediate risks. Outreach cannot force help or guarantee a shelter bed.
Philadelphia Office of Homeless Services

entries.title: Office of Homeless Services
entries.description:
Questions: 215-686-7175. Prevention information: 215-686-7177, recorded message.
Ask about shelter intake, homelessness prevention, family needs, or how to correct a problem with a city-funded homeless service. Funding and placement are not guaranteed.
City of Philadelphia — services for people experiencing homelessness

entries.title: 211 Southeastern Pennsylvania
entries.description:
Call: 211 or 866-964-7922. Text: 898211. — sms:898211
Ask for a meal, pantry, shelter, benefits, health care, rent help, utility help, or another local service. Give your ZIP code or nearest cross streets and ask what is open today.
211 Southeastern Pennsylvania

entries.title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
entries.description:
Call or text: 988. Philadelphia crisis line: 215-685-6440.
Use these lines for suicidal thoughts, an emotional crisis, or an urgent mental-health or substance-use concern. Call 911 when there is immediate physical danger.
Healthy Minds Philly — crisis support

entries.title: Code Blue cold-weather response
entries.description:
Philadelphia may activate Code Blue when precipitation and temperature or dangerous wind chill create a serious cold risk. During an activation, call Street Outreach at 215-232-1984 for someone outdoors.
Rules and locations can change with the weather. Do not wait for an official activation if a person is confused, very drowsy, shivering uncontrollably, or has pale or numb skin; call 911.
City of Philadelphia — Code Blue help

entries.title: A practical plan for today
entries.description:
1. If there is immediate danger or a medical emergency, call 911. For a mental-health or substance-use crisis without immediate physical danger, call or text 988.
2. For someone living outdoors, call 215-232-1984. For a shelter request, use daytime city intake or the after-hours location matching the household.
3. Ask intake for a backup plan, safe waiting place, and transportation if there is no bed. During severe cold, ask whether Code Blue is active.
4. For food, showers, laundry, mail, and health care today, check Hub of Hope, Broad Street Love, The Center Philadelphia, or Prevention Point. Arrive early.
5. Use BenePhilly for benefits, PA CareerLink for work, Homeless Advocacy Project for identification or civil legal help, and the tenant hotline for eviction.
6. Write down each program, the person you spoke with, time, next step, and documents requested. Photograph papers when possible and keep every court or benefit deadline.
If a listing is wrong or has changed: use the contribution link below and include the provider's official source. Do not publish a survivor's confidential address or anyone's personal information.

entries.title: City shelter intake — what to expect
entries.description:
City intake staff assess safety, household composition, health, disability, veteran status, and possible alternatives to shelter. They may connect people to shelter, medical or behavioral-health care, treatment, child services, case management, or supportive housing. No assessment guarantees placement.
The city says a household should not be denied shelter entrance solely because it lacks identification, a birth certificate, or guardianship document. Bring papers if available, but do not delay an urgent request because they are missing.
City of Philadelphia — find emergency housing

entries.title: Appletree Family Center — daytime intake
entries.description:
Phone: 215-686-7150, 215-686-7151, or 215-686-7153. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 7:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Daytime shelter and diversion assessment. Explain every household member and any medical, disability, language, pregnancy, safety, or transportation need.
City of Philadelphia — intake locations
entries.address: Address: 1430 Cherry Street, Philadelphia, PA 19102

entries.title: Roosevelt Darby Center — daytime intake
entries.description:
Phone: 215-685-3700. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 7:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Daytime shelter and diversion assessment. Arrive as early as possible and ask for written directions to the next site if staff refer you elsewhere.
City of Philadelphia — emergency housing
entries.address: Address: 804 N. Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19130

entries.title: Red Shield Family Residence — families after hours
entries.description:
Phone: 215-787-2887. Published intake: weekdays 5:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m.; holidays and weekends.
After-hours intake for families. Space is not guaranteed. Tell staff if anyone is a minor, pregnant, ill, disabled, fleeing violence, or without a safe place that night.
City of Philadelphia — after-hours family intake
entries.address: Address: 715 N. Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19123

entries.title: ACTS After Hour Intake — families
entries.description:
Phone: 267-297-7870. Published intake: weekdays 5:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m.; 24 hours on holidays and weekends.
Another after-hours family intake location. Call when possible to confirm where to go and ask about transportation if the household cannot reach the site safely.
City of Philadelphia — after-hours intake
entries.address: Address: 1300 E. Tulpehocken Street, Philadelphia, PA 19138

entries.title: Mike Hinson Resource Center — single men after hours
entries.description:
Phone: 267-737-9099. Published intake: 3:00–11:00 p.m.; holidays and weekends.
After-hours intake for single men. Ask what time to arrive, whether transport is available, and what to do if capacity is full.
City of Philadelphia — single-adult intake
entries.address: Address: 1701 W. Lehigh Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19132

entries.title: Gaudenzia House of Passage — single women after hours
entries.description:
Phone: 267-713-7778. Published intake: weekdays 5:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m.; holidays and weekends.
After-hours intake for single women. The city says people may use the center that most closely fits their gender identity.
City of Philadelphia — after-hours women's intake
entries.address: Address: 111 N. 49th Street, entrance at 48th Street and Haverford Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19139

entries.title: Covenant House Pennsylvania — ages 18–24
entries.description:
Phone: 215-951-5411. Access: walk-in, 24 hours.
Emergency shelter and support for young adults ages 18–24, including food, health, education, and career help. The provider states that services are inclusive of LGBTQ+ young people. Capacity and eligibility still apply.
Covenant House Pennsylvania
entries.address: Address: 31 E. Armat Street, Philadelphia, PA 19144

entries.title: Philadelphia Domestic Violence Hotline — confidential shelter
entries.description:
Phone: 866-723-3014, confidential and available 24 hours.
Safety planning, crisis support, interpretation, and possible emergency shelter for survivors and their children. Shelter addresses are confidential and space is limited. Call 911 for immediate danger.
City of Philadelphia — domestic-violence resources

entries.title: Veterans Multi-Service Center — veteran intake
entries.description:
Phone: 215-923-2600. Published shelter assessment: Tuesday and Thursday, 9:00 a.m.–2:00 p.m.
Shelter and diversion assessment for veterans. If the office is closed or travel is impossible, call the national veteran line at 877-424-3838.
City of Philadelphia — veteran intake
entries.address: Address: 213–217 N. 4th Street, Philadelphia, PA 19106

entries.title: City food and meal finder
entries.description:
Phone: call 311 or 211.
Use the city finder or call for the closest free meal or grocery site open today. Ask about the schedule, registration, identification, household limits, and whether food can be carried away.
City of Philadelphia — find free food or meals

entries.title: Broad Street Love — weekday lunch
entries.description:
Phone: 215-735-4847. Published meal: Monday–Friday, 11:30 a.m.–1:15 p.m.
The meal is open to all. Broad Street Love offers optional spiritual support but says it is not a practicing faith community. Its other services continue until 3:00 p.m.
Broad Street Love — services
entries.address: Address: 315 S. Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19107

entries.title: St. Francis Inn Ministries
entries.description:
Phone: 215-423-5845. The provider publishes meals every day of the year, including Monday 4:30–6:00 p.m. and Friday–Sunday 11:30 a.m.–1:00 p.m.
The provider's current page formats some midweek morning times unclearly, so call before relying on Tuesday–Thursday hours. Toiletries, feminine products, diapers, and mail are also available on published schedules.
St. Francis Inn is a Catholic Franciscan ministry. Its services page does not state that worship is required.
St. Francis Inn — ministries and schedule
entries.address: Address: 2441 Kensington Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19125

entries.title: Chosen 300 — Center City meals
entries.description:
Published meals: Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at 6:00 p.m.; Saturday at 5:00 p.m.; Sunday at 9:30 a.m.
Chosen 300 is a Christian organization. Its Sunday page lists worship before the meal; the weekday schedule does not state that worship is a condition of eating. Confirm holiday changes.
Chosen 300 — meal schedule
entries.address: Address: 1116 Spring Garden Street, Philadelphia, PA 19123

entries.title: Chosen 300 — West Philadelphia
entries.description:
Published meals: Monday and Friday at 6:00 p.m.; Sunday at 9:00 a.m. Published groceries: Monday, Tuesday, and Friday, 1:00–2:00 p.m.
Schedules sometimes change for construction or holidays. Check the current provider notice before traveling.
Chosen 300 — West Philadelphia schedule
entries.address: Address: 3959 Lancaster Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19104

entries.title: The Center Philadelphia and Grace Café
entries.description:
Phone: 215-568-6250. Published daytime services: Monday–Thursday, 9:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m.
The daytime program includes a hot meal. Grace Café also publishes a Sunday to-go meal, generally 5:00–6:00 p.m. The church states that people are welcome regardless of spiritual tradition.
The Center Philadelphia — daytime services
entries.address: Address: Arch Street United Methodist Church, 55 N. Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19107

entries.title: Old St. Joseph's Church — coffee and meal
entries.description:
Phone: 215-923-2381. City-published schedule: Tuesday and Thursday, coffee at 10:30 a.m. and meal at 11:00 a.m.
This is a Catholic church. The city meal listing does not state that worship is required. Call before traveling because community-meal schedules can change.
City of Philadelphia — free meal locations
entries.address: Address: 321 Willings Alley, Philadelphia, PA 19106

entries.title: Face to Face — Germantown
entries.description:
Phone: 215-438-7939.
Meals and other basic-needs services are listed by the city and provider. Call for the current meal time and ask about health, legal, clothing, or social-service appointments available that day.
Face to Face Germantown
entries.address: Address: 123 E. Price Street, Philadelphia, PA 19144

categories.title: Day centers, showers, laundry, mail, and clothing

entries.title: Hub of Hope
entries.description:
Phone: 215-309-5225. Published general hours: daily, 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m.
Showers, laundry, clothing, coffee and meals, case management, shelter transport, medical care, behavioral-health care, medication treatment, and medication delivery. Weekday service times differ: the provider publishes last shower appointment at 3:15 p.m., last laundry appointment at 2:15 p.m., and shelter transport from noon to 4:00 p.m.
Dental service is closed until further notice. Arrive early because daily appointments can fill.
Project HOME — Hub of Hope
entries.address: Address: 1400 Arch Street, Sub Concourse; enter near the southeast corner of 15th Street and JFK Boulevard

entries.title: Broad Street Love
entries.description:
Phone: 215-735-4847. Public hours: Monday–Friday, 11:30 a.m.–3:00 p.m.
Mail, clothing, mending, personal-care services, meals, and a concierge desk for benefits, work, shelter, housing, and health referrals. New mailbox sign-up is published for Monday and Thursday, noon–2:00 p.m.
Provider pages list different days for some personal-care services, so ask the front desk for the current schedule.
Broad Street Love — frequently asked questions
entries.address: Address: 315 S. Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19107

entries.title: The Center Philadelphia
entries.description:
Phone: 215-568-6250. Published hours: Monday–Thursday, 9:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m.
Hot meal, showers, laundry, clothing, case management, computer access, and indoor relief. The program is hosted by Arch Street United Methodist Church and welcomes people regardless of religion or spiritual tradition.
The Center Philadelphia — services
entries.address: Address: 55 N. Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19107

entries.title: Prevention Point Philadelphia — Drop-In Center
entries.description:
Phone: 215-634-5272. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 9:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m.
Indoor respite, coffee, clothing, hygiene items, mail, case management, identification and benefits help, substance-use referrals, and shelter navigation. Prevention Point says its shelters do not accept walk-ins; use city intake for a bed request.
Prevention Point — Drop-In Center
entries.address: Address: 2913–2915 Kensington Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19134

entries.title: St. John's Hospice — men
entries.description:
Phone: 215-563-7763.
Day services for men, with meals, showers, clothing, mail, case management, and health connections. Call for the current public schedule before traveling.
St. John's Hospice
entries.address: Address: 1221 Race Street, Philadelphia, PA 19107

categories.title: Health, mental health, and substance-use help

entries.title: Stephen Klein Wellness Center
entries.description:
Phone: 215-320-6187. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Primary care, behavioral health, dental care, pharmacy, reproductive care, and child health. The center uses a sliding fee and states that care is available regardless of ability to pay. Walk-ins may be seen when a provider is available; appointments are safer.
Project HOME — Stephen Klein Wellness Center
entries.address: Address: 2144 Cecil B. Moore Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19121

entries.title: Hub of Hope health clinic
entries.description:
Phone: 215-309-5225. Published medical walk-in: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.
Low-barrier medical care, behavioral-health support, medication treatment for opioid use, and medication delivery. Dental care is currently closed. Walk-in capacity can fill.
Project HOME — Hub of Hope health services
entries.address: Address: 1400 Arch Street, Sub Concourse

entries.title: Community Behavioral Health
entries.description:
Phone: 888-545-2600, 24 hours.
Connection to mental-health and substance-use treatment for Philadelphia Medicaid members and some uninsured residents. Ask for the nearest appropriate assessment or treatment provider.
City of Philadelphia — substance-use treatment

entries.title: Behavioral Health Special Initiative — uninsured residents
entries.description:
Phone: 215-546-1200.
Assessment and connection to substance-use treatment for eligible uninsured or underinsured Philadelphia residents. Treatment depends on clinical assessment, eligibility, and current capacity.
City of Philadelphia — treatment access

entries.title: NET Access Point
entries.description:
Phone: 844-533-8200 or 215-408-4987, 24 hours.
Low-barrier substance-use assessment and connection to treatment, including medication for opioid-use disorder when clinically appropriate. Call 911 for overdose or immediate medical danger.
City of Philadelphia — harm-reduction and treatment resources

entries.title: CareConnect Warmline
entries.description:
Phone: 484-278-1679. Published hours: 9:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m.
Virtual, low-barrier treatment support, including possible buprenorphine care. The city states that insurance is not required. Clinical decisions and prescriptions depend on assessment.
City of Philadelphia — CareConnect information

entries.title: PA Get Help Now
entries.description:
Phone: 800-662-4357, confidential and available 24 hours.
English and Spanish help finding substance-use treatment anywhere in Pennsylvania. Ask about transportation, medication treatment, detoxification, and payment options.
Pennsylvania Department of Drug and Alcohol Programs — Get Help Now

entries.title: Parkway Central Library
entries.description:
Phone: 833-825-5357. Published hours: Monday–Thursday 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.; Friday and Saturday 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; Sunday closed.
Public computers, Wi-Fi, printing, scanning, charging outlets, restrooms, and accessible facilities. Ask staff what can be used without a library card or fixed address. Holiday hours can differ.
Free Library of Philadelphia — Parkway Central
entries.address: Address: 1901 Vine Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103

entries.title: Library social workers
entries.description:
Published availability: Monday–Friday, 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Library social workers can help navigate shelter, benefits, identification, health, and other services. Availability may change, so ask at the information desk.
Free Library — social services
entries.address: Location: Parkway Central Library, 1901 Vine Street

entries.title: Hub of Hope shelter transportation
entries.description:
Published transport hours: Monday–Friday, noon–4:00 p.m.
Transport may be available after shelter coordination. It is not a general free ride and does not guarantee placement. Arrive early and ask what backup route to use.
Project HOME — Hub of Hope
entries.address: Address: 1400 Arch Street, Sub Concourse

entries.title: Low-cost phone and internet help
entries.description:
Ask BenePhilly or a library social worker about current federal Lifeline providers and eligibility. Never give a representative an original identity document or pay for a benefit application.
Federal Lifeline Support

categories.title: Benefits, housing, rent, and utility help

entries.title: BenePhilly
entries.description:
Phone: 800-994-5537.
Free one-on-one help applying for food, health insurance, prescription, disability, utility, and other benefits. A counselor can help complete applications and follow up, but benefit agencies make the final decision.
City of Philadelphia — BenePhilly

entries.title: COMPASS — Pennsylvania benefits
entries.description:
Apply online for SNAP food benefits, Medical Assistance, cash assistance, LIHEAP energy help, and other state programs. Save the confirmation number and copies or photos of uploaded documents.
Online approval is not immediate. BenePhilly or a day center can help if you lack internet, an address, identification, or supporting records.
Pennsylvania COMPASS

entries.title: Homelessness Prevention InfoLine
entries.description:
Recorded information: 215-686-7177.
Information about possible help with rent, move-in costs, utilities, mediation, or emergency travel. Programs depend on eligibility and available funding; the recording or referral does not promise payment.
City of Philadelphia — homelessness prevention

entries.title: Philadelphia tenant and eviction help
entries.description:
Tenant hotline: 267-443-2500.
Call immediately after receiving a rent demand, termination notice, court complaint, lockout threat, or sheriff notice. Free legal advice or representation may be available depending on the case and capacity.
City of Philadelphia — free eviction legal help

entries.title: Zero Fare transit program
entries.description:
The city provides some qualifying residents with free SEPTA travel, but there is no public application. Participants are selected through benefit records or designated community organizations.
Do not pay anyone to apply. Ask a benefit counselor whether another reduced-fare, disability, or senior transit program fits your situation.
City of Philadelphia — Zero Fare questions

entries.title: PA CareerLink Philadelphia — citywide help
entries.description:
Phone: 833-750-5627. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
Job search, career counseling, workshops, hiring events, training referrals, unemployment navigation, and employer connections. Services and training funding do not guarantee employment.
PA CareerLink Philadelphia — locations

entries.title: PA CareerLink — Suburban Station
entries.description:
Phone: 215-557-2592. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
Central-city employment center. Ask about computer access, résumés, identification barriers, training, and employers currently interviewing.
PA CareerLink Philadelphia — Suburban Station
entries.address: Address: 1617 JFK Boulevard, Philadelphia, PA 19103

entries.title: PA CareerLink — West Philadelphia
entries.description:
Phone: 215-473-3630. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
Employment and training assistance. Bring identification and a résumé if available, but ask staff what services can begin when documents are missing.
PA CareerLink Philadelphia — West
entries.address: Address: 5548 Chestnut Street, Suite 101, Philadelphia, PA 19139

entries.title: PA CareerLink — North Philadelphia
entries.description:
Phone: 215-967-9711. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
Job search and training support. Ask about same-day workshops, computer access, and employers open to applicants with gaps, limited experience, or a record.
PA CareerLink Philadelphia — North
entries.address: Address: 4261 N. 5th Street, Philadelphia, PA 19140

entries.title: Broad Street Love — employment navigation
entries.description:
Concierge hours: Monday–Friday, 11:30 a.m.–3:00 p.m.
Ask the concierge desk for help connecting to work, benefits, identification, health, shelter, or housing resources. It is a navigation service, not a job placement guarantee.
Broad Street Love — concierge services
entries.address: Address: 315 S. Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19107

entries.title: Homeless Advocacy Project
entries.description:
Phone: 215-523-9595 or 800-837-2672.
Free civil legal help for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Ask about identification, SSI or SSDI, other benefits, family issues, records, or housing. The program cannot accept every case.
Homeless Advocacy Project — get help
entries.address: Address: 1429 Walnut Street, 15th Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19102

entries.title: Weekly HAP clinic at Broad Street Love
entries.description:
Published clinic: Wednesday, 11:30 a.m.–2:00 p.m.
Walk-in legal clinic through the Homeless Advocacy Project. Arrive early with every notice, court paper, benefit letter, identification record, and deadline. Clinic capacity can fill.
Broad Street Love — legal services
entries.address: Address: 315 S. Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19107

entries.title: Philadelphia Eviction Prevention Project
entries.description:
Tenant hotline: 267-443-2500.
Legal information and possible representation for tenants facing eviction. Call as soon as a notice arrives; do not miss a hearing while waiting for a return call. Keep the lease, notices, payment proof, messages, photos, and court papers.
City of Philadelphia — eviction legal help

entries.title: Protection from Abuse order — weekday filing
entries.description:
Phone: 215-686-3512. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
A Protection from Abuse order can address safety from an intimate partner or family member. Filing has no fee. Call the domestic-violence hotline for confidential planning and 911 for immediate danger.
Philadelphia Police — victim resources and PFA information
entries.address: Address: Family Court, 1501 Arch Street, 8th Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19102

entries.title: Emergency Protection from Abuse order — nights and weekends
entries.description:
Phone: 215-683-7280. Published access: 5:00 p.m.–8:00 a.m., weekends, and holidays.
Emergency after-hours PFA filing. Ask the domestic-violence hotline how to reach the correct entrance and make a safe plan for travel.
Philadelphia Police — emergency PFA information
entries.address: Address: Criminal Justice Center, 1301 Filbert Street, Room B-26, Philadelphia, PA 19107

entries.title: Free Pennsylvania photo ID for people experiencing homelessness
entries.description:
Pennsylvania waives the initial or renewal photo-ID fee for a person experiencing homelessness. A PennDOT Driver License Center uses Form DL-54A and may require identity and residency confirmation from a shelter or service provider.
Rules differ for replacement cards, driver-license reinstatement, or missing underlying documents. Ask Homeless Advocacy Project for help before paying anyone.
PennDOT — get a photo ID

entries.title: Homeless Advocacy Project — document help
entries.description:
Phone: 215-523-9595 or 800-837-2672.
Free civil legal help for people experiencing or facing homelessness, including identification documents, public benefits, family matters, and access to records. Eligibility and capacity apply.
Homeless Advocacy Project
entries.address: Address: 1429 Walnut Street, 15th Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19102

entries.title: Broad Street Love — mailing address
entries.description:
Published new mailbox sign-up: Monday and Thursday, noon–2:00 p.m. Mail access: Monday–Friday, 11:30 a.m.–3:00 p.m.
Ask what name, identification, and collection rules apply before using the address on benefit, court, employer, or health forms.
Broad Street Love — mail questions
entries.address: Address: 315 S. Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19107

entries.title: Prevention Point — mail, ID, and benefits navigation
entries.description:
Phone: 215-634-5272.
Ask the Drop-In Center about receiving mail, replacing identification, benefits applications, and document storage practices. Availability may depend on enrollment and staff capacity.
Prevention Point — Drop-In Center
entries.address: Address: 2913–2915 Kensington Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19134

categories.title: Domestic violence, sexual violence, and gender-specific help

entries.title: Philadelphia Domestic Violence Hotline
entries.description:
Phone: 866-723-3014, confidential and available 24 hours.
Safety planning, crisis counseling, interpretation, and access to emergency shelter or other services for survivors and their children. The hotline serves people of any gender. Shelter space is not guaranteed.
City of Philadelphia — domestic-violence resources

entries.title: Women Against Abuse Legal Center
entries.description:
Free legal help may be available for Protection from Abuse orders, custody, and support matters connected to domestic violence. Begin with the 24-hour hotline at 866-723-3014 for safe referral.
Women Against Abuse — Legal Center

entries.title: WOAR Philadelphia Center Against Sexual Violence
entries.description:
24-hour hotline: 215-985-3333.
Confidential crisis counseling and support after sexual assault or abuse. Call 911 for immediate danger. A survivor can ask about medical care, evidence collection, reporting choices, accompaniment, and counseling without being forced to make every decision at once.
WOAR Philadelphia Center Against Sexual Violence

entries.title: Gender identity at city shelter intake
entries.description:
The city states that a person is welcome to use the intake center that most closely fits their gender identity. Tell staff privately about safety, medication, mobility, or accommodation needs and ask for a supervisor if a problem occurs.
City of Philadelphia — emergency housing access

entries.title: Covenant House — LGBTQ+ inclusive youth shelter
entries.description:
Phone: 215-951-5411.
The provider states that its services for ages 18–24 are inclusive of LGBTQ+ young people. Ask about current shelter capacity, safety, health care, identification, education, and work support.
Covenant House Pennsylvania
entries.address: Address: 31 E. Armat Street, Philadelphia, PA 19144

categories.title: Families, youth, older adults, and disability needs

entries.title: Families with children — city intake
entries.description:
Use Appletree Family Center or Roosevelt Darby Center on weekday daytime hours. After hours, use Red Shield Family Residence or ACTS. Tell staff every child's age, school, medications, disability needs, pregnancy, and safety concern.
Do not delay urgent intake because identification, birth certificates, or guardianship papers are missing. Bring any documents you have.
City of Philadelphia — family emergency housing

entries.title: Eddie's House — young adults ages 18–24
entries.description:
Phones: 215-921-8375 or 215-307-3273. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 10:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.
Youth access points for housing assessment and connections. Call to confirm which location to use and what services are available that day.
City of Philadelphia — youth access points
entries.address: Locations: 2321 N. Broad Street and 5901 Market Street, Philadelphia

entries.title: Synergy Project at Valley Youth House — ages 14–24
entries.description:
Phones: 888-468-7315 or 215-925-3180. Published hours: Monday–Thursday 8:30 a.m.–5:30 p.m.; Friday 8:30 a.m.–3:00 p.m.
Hygiene, showers, clothing, food, housing assessment, education and job help, and mental-health referrals for young people. Call ahead if under 18 or seeking overnight shelter.
City of Philadelphia — youth services
entries.address: Address: 1880 JFK Boulevard, Suite 660, Philadelphia, PA 19103

entries.title: School rights for students experiencing homelessness
entries.description:
Children and youth without stable housing have a right to free public education and may be able to enroll immediately even when residency or school records are missing. Ask the school counselor for the district's McKinney-Vento liaison and discuss school-of-origin options.
School District of Philadelphia — student rights

entries.title: Philadelphia Corporation for Aging — age 60 and older
entries.description:
Helpline: 215-765-9040. Main office: 642 N. Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19130.
Service navigation for adults age 60 and older, including meals, care, housing-related support, and emergency needs. For suspected abuse, neglect, exploitation, or serious self-neglect, choose option 1; that response is available 24 hours.
Philadelphia Corporation for Aging — help and questions

entries.title: Disability, mobility, and medical needs
entries.description:
Tell intake staff about wheelchairs, oxygen, medications needing refrigeration, communication needs, a recent hospital discharge, pregnancy, or a trained service animal. Ask which site can safely meet the need and whether transportation is available.
Call 911 for a life-threatening medical condition. For non-emergency care, contact Stephen Klein Wellness Center at 215-320-6187.
City of Philadelphia — shelter assessment

entries.title: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans
entries.description:
Phone: 877-424-3838, free, confidential, and available 24 hours.
Connection to VA homelessness programs, health care, housing, benefits, and local services. Veterans and people calling on a veteran's behalf may use the line. A referral does not guarantee immediate housing.
U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs — call center

entries.title: Philadelphia VA Community Resource and Referral Center
entries.description:
Phone: 215-222-7465 or 215-823-5800, extension 207465.
Published program hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00–11:30 a.m. and 1:00–3:00 p.m. Housing, health, mental-health, career, and benefit connections for veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness.
VA — Community Resource and Referral Centers
entries.address: Address: 213 N. 4th Street, 2nd Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19106

entries.title: Veterans Multi-Service Center
entries.description:
Phone: 215-923-2600. City-published shelter assessment: Tuesday and Thursday, 9:00 a.m.–2:00 p.m.
Ask about emergency shelter assessment, housing, employment, benefits, and supportive services. Bring military records if available, but call even if documents are missing.
Veterans Multi-Service Center
entries.address: Address: 213–217 N. 4th Street, Philadelphia, PA 19106

entries.title: PAWS Pet Owner Support
entries.description:
Philadelphia residents can request pet food, supplies, affordable veterinary care, transport, or temporary safety-net foster care for cats and dogs. Foster capacity is limited and PAWS cannot accept every request.
PAWS — Pet Owner Support

entries.title: ACCT Philly pet resource portal
entries.description:
Links to pet food, low-cost veterinary care, Safe Havens for Pets, temporary foster care, and limited short-term boarding. Each program has its own eligibility, capacity, and reclaim rules.
Do not abandon or surrender an animal based only on an online listing. Contact the program and make a confirmed plan first.
ACCT Philly — help keeping a pet

entries.title: Service animals and shelter planning
entries.description:
Tell shelter intake staff that you have a trained service animal and describe the disability-related tasks it performs. Pets and emotional-support animals may be handled under different rules, so ask before traveling and request a supervisor if an accommodation problem occurs.
For a pet that is not a trained service animal, contact PAWS or ACCT before surrendering it. No temporary-care option is guaranteed.
U.S. Department of Justice — service-animal rights
